thesis: Pinterest, Inc. (NYSE: PINS), visual discovery advertising platform. Q3 2026 (release 2026-10-29): revenue 1,173.9M (+12%), MAU 661M (+10%), global ARPU 1.80 (+1%), US and Canada ARPU 8.38 (+10%), adjusted EBITDA 339.2M (+11%, 29% margin), GAAP net income 21.5M (vs 92.1M), non-GAAP EPS 0.46. Q4 guide revenue 1,425-1,475M (+8-12%), adjusted EBITDA 538-588M. TTM FCF about 1.26B is an 11.5% yield on a 10.98B market cap at 19.15 (2026-11-13 close, 52-week 13.84-27.96), but TTM SBC is 1.08B so FCF after SBC is only about 0.18B (1.7%) and trailing GAAP P/E is about 80x. In 2026 the company cut under 15% of staff, bought tvScientific for 465.1M, issued a 1.0B convertible to Elliott affiliates and spent 2.0B on repurchases including a 1.0B ASR. Net cash is about 0.49B. The market may be pricing slowing monetization and heavy dilution; the evidence is that cash generation is real but mostly reflects non-cash pay, so cheapness depends on whether SBC is treated as a cost.
counterthesis: SBC of 847.7M in nine months (about 25% of revenue) is a real cost: buybacks of 2.0B in 2026 largely offset dilution and equity fell 35%. GAAP operating income was negative for 9M26 (-105M), net loss 98.7M. Global ARPU grew only 1% and Europe ARPU fell 7%; Q4 growth guide decelerates to 8-12%; competition from Meta, Google, Amazon and AI search shifts. The 1.0B convertible is related-party debt at 1.75% with cap-call cost; the 2026 acquisition added goodwill. A stock that fell 41% from a year ago and sits near the low end of its range is not cheap on SBC-adjusted earnings. Forms 144 sales continue (content unread).
invalidation: Thesis breaks if revenue growth drops below the 8% guide floor, ARPU declines globally, SBC keeps above 20% of revenue while buybacks fail to offset share count, or free cash flow after SBC stays near zero.
